messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident PD-8234 fired — synthetic heatmap probes (eu-west-1) showing a spike in failures across probe shards. 17 failing probes in the last 5m. Link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD-8234

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: Triggered by check 'synth-heatmap-euw' (severity: critical) — auto-escalation in 3m if unacked.

maria: acked on behalf of standby. I'm taking first triage. quick check: are these true 5xxs or probe timeouts?

kevin: seeing 502/504s in the probe logs, but tailing the origin shows 429s from our edge WAF in front of prober fleet. suspect rate-limiting noise.

ashley: noted — last deploy to edge firewall was 15m ago (rule id: fw-2026-03-14-a). Could be related. Can someone confirm correlation by timestamp?

ryan: running quick query against synth logs:```json
{
  "probe":"synth-heatmap-euw",
  "start":"2026-03-14T10:12:00Z",
  "errors_by_code": {"429": 43, "502": 3}
}
```

maria: ok 429s dominate. That explains the probe failures; upstream WAF started throttling our prober IP blocks. low-customer-impact so far (no current customer 5xx increase seen in APM). marking as likely false-positive but still noisy pager.

incident-bot: PagerDuty reminder: PD-8234 will escalate to Tier2 in 2m if not acknowledged by another responder.

kevin: I'll silence the pager for this check while we mitigate. Plan: 1) add temporary prober IP whitelist on WAF, 2) backfill prober requests with randomized backoff, 3) lower probe fanout for 10m.

ashley: +1. I'll open a support ticket with firewall team to rollback the aggressive rule. tagging @firewall-team.

maria: executing manual silence: ```# mute synth-heatmap-euw for 15m
curl -X POST "https://api.pagerduty.com/rules/mute" -H "Authorization: Token token=REDACTED" -d '{"service":"synth-heatmap-euw","duration":15}'
```

pagerduty: ACK recorded: user maria (standby) — silence applied for 15m. Auto-escalation suppressed.

ops-bot: Prober control: lowering fanout for synth-heatmap-euw to 0.25x for 10m. New config: `probe_fanout_multiplier: 0.25`

ryan: firewall ticket created: FW-1879 — requested immediate rollback of rule fw-2026-03-14-a, flagged as Sev-1 for potential internal impact. Link: https://fw.example/tickets/FW-1879

kevin: I applied a temporary WAF allowlist entry for prober CIDR (10.200.0.0/22) — should stop the 429s. Monitoring metrics now.

maria: watching synth dashboard — failures drop to 1 in the last 3m. thumbs up.

oncall-next: thanks team. I'll take the handoff — will monitor for another 30m then unmute. please add a short postmortem note if the firewall rule was root cause.

maria: adding notes to PD-8234: root cause likely WAF throttling prober IPs due to new rule fw-2026-03-14-a. Mitigations: WAF allowlist added, prober fanout reduced, pager silenced. Action items: firewall rollback or tuned rule, permanent allowlist for prober fleet, add prober IP health check to deploy gating.

kevin: creating ticket in infra-postmortems: PM-1024 with timeline and links (PD-8234, FW-1879).

incident-bot: PD-8234 updated: status = acknowledged, responders = [maria], urgency = low (post-mitigations).

maria: closing loop — no customer-facing errors observed, marking customer impact = none. leaving monitoring to oncall-next.

oncall-next: taking over. will unmute after 30m and confirm stable. :thumbsup:
